title: End-to-end encrypted calls with key-derived identities
summary:
Implemented real identity + end-to-end encryption for the relay voice-call app.

- crypto.js: Ed25519 identity (generateIdentity/loadIdentity/fingerprint/verify) and per-call X25519 + AES-GCM E2E via CallSession (initiator/responder/completeInitiator/encrypt/decrypt), with Node-compat fallbacks.
- server.js: register→challenge→auth handshake; id must equal fingerprint(pubkey), then challenge signed with the private key; same-key reconnect evicts the stale socket, different key claiming an online id is rejected (id-taken); signal now carries signed offer/answer key material; dropped `name` from protocol.
- relay.js: connect(id, token, auth), answers the server challenge, sends signed offer/answer on call/accept.
- main.js: derives the peer ID from the public key, persists identity, wires CallSession into startCall/acceptIncomingInternal/handleAccepted, encrypts every sent frame and decrypts every received frame (serialized chains), surfaces id-taken instead of rotating the id.
- Aligned all test suites (server, server-unit, token, relay, main, util) to the new protocol; full suite is green at 308 tests across 10 files.
- Repo hygiene: removed dead generateId (identity is now key-derived), deleted orphan src/rnnoise.wasm (denoiser is FastEnhancer DTLN loaded from src/assets), ignored graphify-out/ and .cursor/, replaced 7 @illusion TODO placeholder comments with real descriptions, and documented the crypto model in README (Security section) while fixing the outdated RNNoise→FastEnhancer DTLN naming.
userVisibleChange: Calls are now end-to-end encrypted and identities are unforgeable: your peer ID is the fingerprint of your Ed25519 public key, and every call sets up an ephemeral X25519 + AES-GCM session the relay cannot read. The README documents the security model.

risks.title: Relay sees metadata in cleartext
risks.mitigation: Who-calls-whom, call timing, and mute state are visible to the relay by design; audio content and identities' private keys are not. Documented in README.

decisions.title: Peer ID = fingerprint of public key
decisions.rationale: SHA-256(pubkey)[:12] base32 gives a short, copy-pasteable, unforgeable ID; only the private-key holder can register it.

decisions.title: Registration = challenge/response
decisions.rationale: Server issues a random nonce; client signs it with Ed25519, proving possession of the private key for the claimed id.

decisions.title: E2E via signed ephemeral X25519
decisions.rationale: Per-call ephemeral keypair, signed and verified against the peer's fingerprint, prevents key-swap MITM; HKDF splits into per-direction AES-GCM keys.

decisions.title: Drop `name` from the protocol
decisions.rationale: Call names are local contact labels and were never sensitive; removing them simplifies the protocol and avoids leaking them.
